STEP 1 - Scene: A salad-style plate of fresh baby spinach leaves with a few corn kernels/pieces and a bit of scallion or green onion. It appears to be a side salad or starter.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A large square white plate, roughly 26 cm across. Area ≈ 3.14 × (13)² ≈ 530 cm². The partial plate at the left edge (with a fork and a bit of food) is a separate place setting and is excluded.

STEP 3 - Items:
- Fresh spinach leaves (main bulk)
- Corn (one cut-off cob piece, plus scattered kernels)
- Green onion / scallion pieces (small)

STEP 4 - Area:
- Spinach leaves: ~38% of vessel (≈200 cm²)
- Corn cob piece: ~4% (≈22 cm²)
- Scallion pieces and scattered kernels: ~1% (≈5 cm²)
Total covered ≈ 43%, which is a plausible share for a pile in the center of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Spinach: 200 cm² × 3.5 cm (loose pile, tall) ≈ 700 ml
- Corn: 22 cm² × 3 cm ≈ 66 ml
- Scallion: 5 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 8 ml

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Spinach: 700 ml × 0.15 g/ml ≈ 105 g
- Corn: 66 ml × 0.6 ≈ 40 g (kernels plus cob-core; the cob core is inedible, so keep the estimate modest, about 30 g edible)
- Scallion: 8 ml × 0.5 ≈ 4 g

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Spinach: 105 g × 23 kcal/100 g ≈ 24 kcal
- Corn: 30 g × 86 kcal/100 g ≈ 26 kcal
- Scallion: 4 g × 32 kcal/100 g ≈ 1 kcal
Total ≈ 51 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A fairly sparse pile of spinach with one corn piece on a 26 cm plate. About 140 g total and roughly 50 kcal is plausible for a small side salad with no dressing visible. No oil or dressing sheen is apparent.
